title: Cyrus and the Gravity
premise: Ulyana Marchetti smuggles memories past orbital customs and keeps the beacon lit on a station nobody claims, hiding from both sides of a war that would use her cargo as a weapon. When the derelict ship Perihelion returns from deep space with its crew aged backward into children who remember the future, Ulyana learns her beacon is actually a receiver — and it has been holding a message meant to end the war before either side can weaponize time itself. Pursued by the Admiralty's memory-hunters and the rebel cartel she once betrayed, Ulyana must choose between delivering the message (which will expose her own erased past) or destroying it to keep her found family safe. She delivers it, sacrificing her anonymity and nearly her life, and the ceasefire holds — but the message reveals she was the one who sent it, decades from now.
about_author: Zephyrine Vasquez is a former radio astronomer who left observatory life to write fiction about signals no one wants to hear. She lives aboard a decommissioned ferry in a northern harbor, where she claims the tides help her plot.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Ulyana runs contraband memories through customs using forged grief-records, then climbs to maintain the station's orphaned beacon. POV: Ulyana. Beat: weary competence masking loneliness; establishes her rule — stay invisible, stay alive.

chapters.title: Cargo That Breathes
chapters.summary: A client pays triple for a sealed memory-capsule Ulyana is forbidden to open. Her partner, the ex-navigator Dov, urges caution; her ward, teen pilot Sefa, wants the money. POV: Ulyana. Beat: temptation and the first crack in invisibility.

chapters.title: Perihelion Returns
chapters.summary: A ship thought lost for thirty years docks without hailing — crewed by children wearing veterans' faces grown young. They speak in unison fragments of a message addressed to 'the keeper of the light.' POV: Sefa. Beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Children Who Remember Tomorrow
chapters.summary: Ulyana interrogates the eldest child, Captain Ilsa Rehn aged down to nine, who recalls Ulyana's face from a future she shouldn't remember. The Admiralty's salvage claim arrives within hours. POV: Ilsa. Beat: uncanny intimacy; the trap begins closing.

chapters.title: Customs, and Other Predators
chapters.summary: Inspector Vey of the Admiralty boards under pretense of quarantine, scanning for temporal contraband. Ulyana hides the children among smuggled memories, literally inside stolen recollections. POV: Ulyana. Beat: cat-and-mouse tension; love for the kids overrules self-preservation.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Is For
chapters.summary: Dov decodes the beacon's maintenance logs: it isn't a transmitter but a locked receiver, keyed to a cipher only Ulyana's own erased childhood matches. Someone built her into this station. POV: Dov. Beat: revelation and vertigo — Ulyana's identity was engineered.

chapters.title: The Cartel Sends Regards
chapters.summary: Rebel memory-broker Ossian Kade, whom Ulyana betrayed years ago, arrives demanding the Perihelion's cargo as payment of old debts. He offers protection at a price: the message, intact. POV: Ulyana. Beat: old wounds reopened; power as seduction.

chapters.title: Sefa's Choice
chapters.summary: Sefa, starved for belonging, secretly offers Kade the children's location in exchange for a place in his fleet. She finds his loyalty rituals intoxicating and hollow. POV: Sefa. Beat: corruption's gentle entry; betrayal born of loneliness.

chapters.title: Aged Backward
chapters.summary: Ilsa explains the deep-space anomaly: a gravity well where time pools backward, and the message is a recording of the well's coordinates — a weapon if militarized, a peace if broadcast honestly. POV: Ilsa. Beat: stakes clarified; innocence carrying terrible knowledge.

chapters.title: Vey's Offer
chapters.summary: Inspector Vey privately tells Ulyana the Admiralty will erase the children rather than study them, and offers her amnesty to hand them over. She recognizes the erasure procedure — it's what was done to her. POV: Vey. Beat: antagonist humanized; duty shown as another kind of corruption.

chapters.title: Erased
chapters.summary: Ulyana opens her own sealed memory-capsule, the one she's carried unopened for fifteen years, and relives her recruitment as the beacon's keeper — and the family taken from her when she refused to weaponize it once before. POV: Ulyana. Beat: devastating midpoint reversal; grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Fleet Comes to Station Kestrel
chapters.summary: Both the Admiralty squadron and Kade's cartel converge on the station. Dov rigs the docks to fail while Ulyana moves the children through the memory-vaults' sensory maze. POV: Dov. Beat: siege pressure; quiet heroism.

chapters.title: Inside a Stolen Memory
chapters.summary: Trapped in a contraband memory of someone else's wedding, Ulyana and Ilsa hide while hunters pass close enough to touch. Ilsa asks whether the future can be forgiven in advance. POV: Ulyana. Beat: tenderness under mortal danger; love against duty crystallizes.

chapters.title: Kade Collects
chapters.summary: Kade seizes the beacon chamber and tortures Dov for the cipher key. Sefa, watching, realizes what his 'family' costs. POV: Sefa. Beat: horror and disillusionment; the theme of corrupted power made flesh.

chapters.title: The Cipher Is a Name
chapters.summary: Ulyana surrenders herself to stop the torture, then speaks her birth-name into the receiver — the key all along. The message unlocks and begins broadcasting to both fleets simultaneously. POV: Ulyana. Beat: sacrifice as agency; rising toward climax.

chapters.title: Two Fleets Listen
chapters.summary: The message plays: proof that the time-well cannot be owned, only survived, plus a peace framework signed by leaders not yet born. Vey must choose between orders and evidence. POV: Vey. Beat: climax approaches; an enemy converts.

chapters.title: Firefight at the Light
chapters.summary: Kade tries to jam the broadcast and seize the children as leverage; station defenses, Dov's sabotage, and defecting customs officers collide in the beacon chamber. Sefa turns on Kade to save Ilsa. POV: Sefa. Beat: violent climax; redemption earned through cost.

chapters.title: Gravity Wins
chapters.summary: Kade falls — pulled into the beacon's exposed temporal field, aging decades in seconds, undone by the power he sought. The broadcast completes. Both fleets stand down under mutual blackmail of truth. POV: Ulyana. Beat: catharsis; corruption destroyed by its own appetite.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Message
chapters.summary: Ceasefire negotiators arrive; the children are promised guardianship, not dissection. Vey burns her report on Ulyana's origins, choosing complicity in mercy over duty in cruelty. POV: Vey. Beat: exhale; small justices.

chapters.title: Growing Forward
chapters.summary: Ilsa and the crew-children begin re-aging under the station's care, their futures uncertain but theirs again. Sefa formally joins the household, forgiven. POV: Ilsa. Beat: healing; belonging chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Signature
chapters.summary: Dov decrypts the message's final metadata layer: authorship timestamped forty years ahead, signed with Ulyana's name. She sent it — will send it — from the well itself. POV: Ulyana. Beat: awe and dread braided; destiny reframed as choice pending.

chapters.title: Cyrus and the Gravity
chapters.summary: Naming the beacon Cyrus after the child-captain's forgotten middle name, Ulyana refits the Perihelion for one voluntary voyage back to the well — to become the sender, on her terms. She leaves the light burning for whoever comes next. POV: Ulyana. Beat: resolution with an open horizon; love chosen over safety, duty rewritten as devotion.
